newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hopewell plans funding for Thai project.
newsitem.headline: Hopewell plans funding for Thai project.

text.p: Hong Kong-based infrastructure firm Hopewell Holdings Ltd said on Friday it was looking at equity funding of about US$1 billion and project financing of over US$2 billion for its US$3.2 billion mass transit project in Bangkok.
"We have spent almost, but not yet, US$500 million on the project. And of course we will be putting in extra equity into the project," executive director Robert Niem told a news conference.
"We are looking possibly at around US$1 billion for the BERTS (Bangkok Elevated Road and Train System) equity and the rest will be by project finance on a limited recourse basis," he said.
"I think we will be putting in the extra equity over the next 12 months," he added.
"The financing is you know very very large. we are looking at over US$2 billion worth of project finance," he said.
But the financing would take at least several months to finalise, he said.
Niem said he expected no difficulty in seeking such loans and the BERTS project would be able to meet its schedule.
"There has been substantial interest in international banks to arrange the project finance. And so far we've made some progress," he added.
The project includes a freeway, an elevated train system and the upgrading and elevating of part of the existing state railway system in Bangkok, Thailand.
